title: Antenatal Fetal Surveillance
keywords: BPP 5 components NST breathing movement tone AFV
umbilical artery S/D ratio < 3 after 30 weeks
sources: Critical Vector — OB Pocket Guide: Fetal Surveillance (ACOG 2024)
ACOG Practice Bulletins on antepartum fetal surveillance and fetal growth restriction; SMFM

changelog.change: Initial entry — BPP scoring and action, umbilical artery Doppler interpretation, FGR definitions and delivery triggers.

summary: The biophysical profile scores five components 0 or 2 each (total 0–10). An abnormal umbilical artery Doppler is the trigger for escalated surveillance in fetal growth restriction — absent end-diastolic flow means delivery by 34 weeks, and reversed flow means delivery now regardless of gestation.

rows: ≥ 1 episode of active extension–flexion of a limb or trunk in 30 min
AFI ≥ 5 cm, OR a single deepest pocket ≥ 2 cm
Normal — repeat per the indication (twice weekly for most high-risk conditions)
Equivocal — deliver if ≥ 37 wk; if preterm, repeat in 24 h and consider steroids
Abnormal — delivery strongly considered regardless of gestation
Deliver at ≥ 36 wk; evaluate for growth restriction and ruptured membranes

body.text: The modified BPP (NST + amniotic fluid) is an acceptable first-line test; a non-reactive NST or low fluid prompts a full BPP.
Umbilical artery Doppler (in fetal growth restriction)

rows: Reassuring; surveillance per the underlying condition
Deliver by 33–34 wk (after steroids); at least daily surveillance if earlier
Deliver as soon as feasible regardless of gestation — impending decompensation

items: Severe FGR: estimated fetal weight < 3rd percentile, OR absent/reversed end-diastolic flow.
FGR: EFW < 10th percentile WITH abnormal Doppler or a concurrent maternal condition.
SGA: EFW < 10th percentile alone with normal Doppler and interval growth — often constitutionally small.
